scope: Proposition 4.3 (The geometric construction) of the manuscript “A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover” (preprints/A-projective-fourfold-with-large-fundamental-group-and-non-Stein-universal-cover-October-5-2026/large-fundamental-group-non-stein.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 046 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 bb2a84e535643f76), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: After any prescribed finite lower bounds on the arrangement radii and injectivity radius, the construction above gives a smooth connected proper effective orbifold S with projective coarse space, a simple abelian surface A = Jac(C), an iterated point blowup Y → A, and a morphism f : Y → S with image in its ordinary locus. The distinguished fiber is obtained from the product C × C, its normal bundle pr∗ 1 L ⊕ pr∗ 2 L, and the action (4.10) by the explicit blowups and coarse quotients above. Away from that fiber the orbifold is [V/⟨s⟩], with V given by the two parity covers and the filling rules of Section 4.4.
